claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness in its simple solid-solution state.
Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low strength in its simple solid-solution state.
The simple solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi alloy has minimal lattice distortion.
The simple solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi alloy lacks nanoscale precipitate barriers.
Minimal lattice distortion and the absence of nanoscale precipitate barriers permit easy dislocation glide.
Easy dislocation glide produces enhanced plasticity and machinability at the expense of strength and hardness.
The starting material is an as-cast, homogeneous, single-phase, equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi solid solution.
A controlled heat treatment can be used to induce nanoscale precipitates and increase lattice distortion in CoCrFeNiTi.
A slight Ti excess or a minor-element addition can promote short-range ordering in CoCrFeNiTi.
Nanoscale precipitates and short-range-order-associated lattice distortions act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
The untreated CoCrFeNiTi solid solution has low lattice friction.
Precipitates and enhanced lattice distortion in modified CoCrFeNiTi will impede dislocation motion.
Modified CoCrFeNiTi will have significantly greater yield strength than the baseline alloy at 25 °C.
Modified CoCrFeNiTi will have significantly greater yield strength than the baseline alloy at 600 °C.
Modified CoCrFeNiTi will have significantly greater hardness than the baseline alloy at both 25 °C and 600 °C.
The increase in strength and hardness will probably be accompanied by reduced plasticity.
The proposed hypothesis is limited to quasi-static loading between 25 °C and 600 °C.
The hypothesis applies only if the intervention does not cause extensive phase segregation or a multiphase microstructure.
TEM and XRD can be used to determine whether the intervention produced precipitates and increased lattice strain.
A failure to obtain a statistically significant increase in hardness and yield strength is specified as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: The intervention and mediator explicitly require formation of nanoscale precipitates, which ordinarily constitute an additional phase, while the boundary says the hypothesis applies only if a multiphase microstructure does not form.
